name: AGC 112521 (Hubble)
blurb: AGC 112521, a gas-rich dwarf galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: agc112521-hubble
story: A tiny, gas-rich dwarf galaxy, among the lowest-mass galaxies that still hold stars, first found by the hydrogen gas it carries. Hubble picked out its brightest red giant stars to measure how far away it is.

claims.text: AGC112521 is a target of Hubble program 12658, 'Fundamental Parameters of the SHIELD Galaxies'
SHIELD galaxies are extremely low-mass, gas-rich galaxies discovered by the ALFALFA radio survey
SHIELD is the Survey of HI in Extremely Low-mass Dwarf galaxies, and all its systems have recent star formation
Hubble program 12658 measured the galaxies' distances with the tip of the red giant branch method
The galaxies were selected from the ALFALFA HI survey (found by their hydrogen gas)
The tip of the red giant branch was detected in AGC 112521
